issues.t: Engine shuts off and shifts into Park on the 5.7L eTorque
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off, usually at low speed or at a stop. The SUV may shift itself into Park and set the parking brake, with a battery warning or low-voltage message. Sometimes it restarts, sometimes it needs a tow.
issues.why: NHTSA opened an investigation (PE24-018) into 2022 Wagoneers and Ram 1500s with the 5.7L eTorque mild-hybrid system after reports of electrical faults shutting the engine down. The eTorque system uses a 48-volt battery and a belt-driven motor-generator in place of a normal alternator. No recall had been announced in the investigation documents.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If it happens, coast to a safe spot and try a restart. Have the dealer read and save the codes, check for software updates and test both the 12-volt and 48-volt batteries.

issues.t: Thermostat sticks closed and the 3.0L overheats
issues.sym: An Engine Overheated message, the temperature gauge jumping around, reduced power mode, a low oil pressure warning or a check engine light. Some owners report coolant loss.
issues.why: A pin inside the thermostat valve on the 3.0L twin-turbo engine can fail, so the thermostat sticks closed and coolant stops reaching the radiator. Stellantis issued a customer satisfaction notice (26B) and then service bulletin 09-006-25 that replaces the thermostat on vehicles built through October 1, 2024.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if it overheats; driving on can blow the head gasket. Ask a dealer whether bulletin 09-006-25 or notice 26B applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Engine stalls or shuts off while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out in traffic, at a light or on the highway. Steering gets heavy, warning lights come on and it may need a restart. Some owners say software updates didn't stop it.
issues.why: Many owners of 2024 models report sudden shutdowns. Dealers have tried software updates and battery work, and no single cause has been confirmed.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Get to a safe place. Note when it happens and have the dealer save the codes right away; ask for a lemon-law log if repeat repairs fail.

issues.t: Shifts into Park or sets the parking brake while moving
issues.sym: The SUV shifts itself into Park or the electronic parking brake applies while rolling or stopped at a light, sometimes after a stall.
issues.why: Owners report this alongside stalls and electrical faults. The system is designed to put the vehicle in Park if it thinks the engine has stopped or the driver is leaving, so an electrical fault can trigger it.
issues.next: Leave room behind you and use hazards if it happens in traffic. Have the dealer save codes and check battery health and software.

issues.t: Battery keeps going dead
issues.sym: The SUV won't start, needs frequent jump starts, or the battery is replaced more than once without a lasting fix.
issues.why: These SUVs have heavy electronic loads and a main and auxiliary battery. Owners report repeated battery failures; dealers have blamed corrosion, the key fob, heat and a faulty liftgate latch.
issues.next: Have both batteries tested and a parasitic draw test done. Keep the key fob away from the vehicle when parked in the garage.

issues.t: Power steering assist cuts out
issues.sym: A power steering warning comes on and the wheel suddenly gets very heavy, on the highway or in slow turns.
issues.why: Owners report loss of electric steering assist, often with other electrical warnings.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Hold the wheel firmly and slow down. Have the dealer read the steering and power codes right away.

issues.t: Brake pedal sinks or braking fades
issues.sym: The brake pedal drops toward the floor with ABS or stability warnings, and the SUV takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Owners report brake assist loss tied to brake system faults. The cause varies.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Use firm, steady pressure and get off the road. Have it towed to a dealer rather than driving it.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking slams on with nothing there
issues.sym: The SUV brakes hard on a clear road or while stopped. A few owners report being rear-ended.
issues.why: The forward collision system can misread its camera or radar. Software and sensor alignment are the usual suspects.
issues.next: Keep the windshield and front sensor clean, and have the dealer check sensor calibration and updates. Report each event to NHTSA.

issues.t: Vibration or wobble at highway speeds
issues.sym: Shaking in the steering wheel or seat above about 65 mph, pulling, or fast tire wear.
issues.why: Owners report vibration that persists after tire balancing and alignments. Wheel, tire and alignment issues are the common checks.
issues.next: Have road-force balancing and an alignment check done, and inspect tires for uneven wear.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure causes stalling
issues.sym: The engine dies, often at speed, and may not restart. Replacement pumps have been back-ordered.
issues.why: A failing fuel pump stops supplying enough fuel.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. If the engine stalls and won't restart, have it towed. Ask the dealer for an estimated parts date and a loaner.

issues.t: Gas smell from fuel leak
issues.sym: A gasoline smell inside or around the SUV, or fuel visible near the injectors or fuel lines.
issues.why: Owners report leaks at the injectors and a fuel line found disconnected.
issues.next: Don't drive it if you smell raw fuel. Have it towed and inspected.

issues.t: Touchscreens freeze, go blank or reboot
issues.sym: The center or passenger screens freeze, reboot, go blank, or a motorized lower screen stays shut. Updates can fail and disable features.
issues.why: Software problems in the infotainment system, which also runs the backup camera and many settings.
issues.next: Try a system restart (hold the power button). Ask the dealer for the latest radio software, including any recall updates.

issues.t: Sun visor breaks or falls down
issues.sym: A sun visor droops, falls into your view or breaks off its clip.
issues.why: Owners report weak visor brackets and clips.
issues.next: Have the visor replaced; it is usually a simple fix under warranty.

issues.t: Seat lumbar support over-inflates
issues.sym: The seat back suddenly hardens or bulges without pressing any button, sometimes on both front seats.
issues.why: A fault in the seat's air lumbar system keeps inflating the bladder.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the lumbar pump and controls. Avoid long drives if it's painful.

issues.t: Climate settings change on their own
issues.sym: Temperature or fan settings change by themselves, or heat output is poor.
issues.why: Owners report software and control glitches in the multi-zone climate system.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about climate control and radio software updates.

issues.t: Air suspension raises or lowers on its own
issues.sym: The ride height changes without input or gets stuck high or low.
issues.why: Faults in the air suspension system, such as a sensor, valve or leak.
issues.next: Have the air suspension codes read and checked for leaks before the compressor wears out.

issues.t: Sunroof glass shatters
issues.sym: The panoramic roof glass breaks suddenly with a loud bang while driving.
issues.why: Owners report the glass shattering without being hit by anything.
issues.next: Pull over safely, cover the opening and contact the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.t: Window trim can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Trim around the rear quarter windows is loose, flaps or falls off while driving.
issues.why: The quarter window trim may not have been secured properly.
issues.next: Have recall 25V-642 done; the dealer replaces the quarter window glass assembly if needed, free.

issues.t: Door trim can come off (recall)
issues.sym: Trim on the front doors is loose or detaches.
issues.why: Door trim may not have been installed properly.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the trim free under recall 25V-593.

issues.t: Roof rack crossbars can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or rattling roof rack crossbars; they could fall off on the road.
issues.why: The pivot bolts for the crossbars may not have been tightened properly.
issues.next: Avoid loading the crossbars until recall 26V-584 is done. The dealer replaces the bolts free.

issues.t: Backup camera image may not appear (recalls)
issues.sym: The screen stays blank or frozen when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: Several recalls cover radio or park-assist software that can block the camera image, and on 2026 models a loose camera wiring connection.
issues.next: Back up carefully using mirrors. Have the dealer or an over-the-air update install every open camera recall. NHTSA recall numbers: 23V-577, 24V-436.

issues.t: Low tire pressure warning may not work (recall)
issues.sym: The tire pressure light may not come on even when a tire is low.
issues.why: A software error in the tire pressure system's receiver hub.
issues.next: Check tire pressures with a gauge monthly until the free software update is done.

issues.t: Stability control and brake assist can switch off (recall)
issues.sym: Stability control or brake assist warnings, and less help in a skid or panic stop.
issues.why: Software in the brake system control module could turn off stability control and electronic brake assist.
issues.next: Drive gently and have the free brake module software update done.

issues.t: Front airbags may be disabled by software (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag light may come on. The front and knee airbags might not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: Incorrect software in the airbag control module.
issues.next: Have the dealer reprogram the airbag module right away. It's free. NHTSA recall number: 21V-873.

issues.t: Driver airbag may not deploy (recall)
issues.sym: Often no warning. The driver airbag might not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: A weld in the steering column control module may be faulty.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the module free under recall 24V-199.

issues.t: Pillar trim can block side curtain airbag (recall)
issues.sym: Loose trim at the top of the middle (B) pillar.
issues.why: The trim may not be fully seated and could get in the way of the curtain airbag.
issues.next: Have the dealer reseat or replace the trim free. NHTSA recall number: 23V-545.

issues.t: Third-row seat belt hard to buckle (recall)
issues.sym: Third-row passengers can't fasten the seat belt properly.
issues.why: The third-row buckle may be positioned or built so it is hard to reach or latch.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect and replace the buckle free. NHTSA recall number: 23V-716.

issues.t: Second-row center seatback may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: The second-row center seatback doesn't latch upright.
issues.why: The recliner strap can bind and keep the seatback from locking.
issues.next: Don't seat anyone there until the dealer replaces the strap free. NHTSA recall number: 21V-919.
